What is RSI?
Think of it like your heart rate right after a run. Too high (overbought) and it may need to cool off; too low (oversold) and it often bounces back.
In plain terms
Above 70 suggests the price may be overheated (overbought).
Below 30 suggests the price may be oversold — often a fear zone.
How to read it
Below 30 signals oversold (fear); above 70 signals overbought (overheated). The middle (30–70) is neutral.
At a glance
RSI is a separate, price-based check that helps you see whether the Fear Index reading lines up with the market\'s technical momentum.
Why it\'s here
A second opinion for the Fear Index
RSI (Relative Strength Index) measures how fast and how much a price has risen or fallen, on a 0–100 scale.
What is RSI?
Price momentum is in neutral territory.
Price is technically overheated too — leaning toward greed.
Price is technically oversold too — leaning toward fear.

What is short selling?
Buying back shares that were sold short. A falling short share signals covering — that repurchasing can spark a short-term bounce.
How to read it
Short-selling trends reveal bearish or rebound sentiment apart from price. It\'s not a standalone trade signal — just a supporting clue for reading the index.
Why we show this
